_readme: Real-photo 360 spins. A turntable is a folder of photographs of one dish,
each shot a fixed number of degrees further around than the last. Playing
them back in order is what makes a real photo appear to rotate.
1. Shoot the dish on a rotating stand — 24 frames (every 15 degrees)
or 36 frames (every 10 degrees, smoother). Camera must not move.
2. Name them 001.jpg, 002.jpg ... in the order they were shot, going
anticlockwise as seen from above (that matches a left-to-right drag).
4. Set frames to how many there are and flip ready to true.
Until ready is true the site falls back to the procedural 3D model, so
nothing is ever blank in front of a customer.
Keep each frame around 1200px wide and under 200KB (JPEG quality ~78).
24 frames at that size is about 4MB — fine to preload on wifi, and the
player loads the first frame instantly and the rest in the background.
